diagrams.title: From Renewal Signal to Retained Contribution
diagrams.subtitle: Five operating steps separate customer subscription spend from earned brokerage revenue.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The operator has customer permission and current vendor agreements. Microsoft CPOR attribution is not interchangeable with CSP resale authority; Adobe VIP Marketplace and Zoom partner routes have their own eligibility and transfer requirements.
diagrams.caption: Track one opportunity identifier across discovery, authorization, quote, activation, and settlement. No stage authorizes cross-customer seat pooling or converts client subscription spend into operator revenue.

stages.label: Detect a renewal trigger
stages.detail: Use public DNS, MX, and SPF signals to prioritize research; confirm actual products, seat counts, and renewal dates from customer-provided contracts rather than inferring license eligibility.

stages.label: Verify the authorized route
stages.detail: Record customer authority and the applicable Microsoft CSP, CPOR, Adobe VIP Marketplace, Zoom Up, or master-agent agreement. Check transfer windows, tenant boundaries, and existing commitments.

stages.label: Price the retained economics
stages.detail: Normalize term, seats, taxes, support, and service levels. Separate vendor-funded spreads from member rebates and 25%–35% shared-savings fees; disclose any combined compensation.

stages.label: Activate and reconcile billing
stages.detail: Complete vendor-approved changes and reconcile Pax8, Ingram, or Telarus records where supported. Fund annual NCE exposure before commitment; monthly auto-debit alone does not cover it.

stages.label: Recognize and monitor earnings
stages.detail: Reconcile partner statements, customer acceptance, rebate conditions, and residual receipts. Apply ASC 606 contract analysis and maintain separate ledgers for client pass-through amounts, operator earnings, and potential reversals.

diagrams.title: A Nested Annual Cohort Supporting the Base Case
diagrams.subtitle: 200 permissioned opportunities narrow to 10 activated portfolio accounts.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Illustrative annual acquisition cohort, not measured conversion data. Each stage is a subset of the preceding stage. Ten portfolio accounts each contribute $50,000 in annual recognized retained revenue after full activation; partial-year activation produces less revenue.
diagrams.caption: Stage conversions are 50%, 50%, 50%, and 40%; overall conversion is 5%. Ten accounts multiplied by $50,000 equals the $500,000 Base-Case annual revenue target. First-deal timing remains 1–3 months.

stages.label: Permissioned opportunities
stages.detail: Count distinct prospective portfolio accounts with an identified buyer, a documented contact basis, and a contract renewal window; exclude scraped contact lists without qualification.

stages.label: Evidence-complete accounts
stages.detail: Half the original cohort supplies invoices, product identifiers, seat counts, commitment dates, and procurement authority sufficient to calculate a comparable incumbent baseline.

stages.label: Eligible economic cases
stages.detail: Half the evidence-complete accounts passes vendor eligibility, minimum retained contribution, and funding checks after migration costs, concessions, and expected clawbacks.

stages.label: Signed mandates
stages.detail: Half the eligible accounts executes a mandate defining compensation, savings measurement, rebate ownership, customer responsibilities, and the permitted licensing route.

stages.label: Activated earning accounts
stages.detail: Forty percent of signed accounts completes activation and begins earning contracted consideration. Treat $500,000 as full-year recognized revenue only when service timing supports it.

diagrams.title: Base-Case Revenue to $225,000 Owner Profit
diagrams.subtitle: $500,000 retained operator revenue less $275,000 operating costs yields 45.0%.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Six bars contain an opening total, four signed deductions, and a closing total; the final bar is not another increment. Cost allocations are illustrative because only scenario totals are canonical. Opening gross revenue is gross within the operator income statement but already net of client subscription pass-through under the specified agency model.
diagrams.caption: $500,000 − $120,000 − $75,000 − $50,000 − $30,000 = $225,000; $225,000 / $500,000 = 45.0%. Conservative is $100,000 revenue, $68,000 costs, and $32,000 profit at 32%. Scaled is $900,000 revenue, $378,000 costs, and $522,000 profit at 58%. The supplied monthly opex range of $1,500–$9,500 is not a ceiling on all-in annual scenario costs.

stages.label: Recognized retained revenue
stages.detail: Count earned partner spreads, master-agent residuals, GPO administrative rebates, and shared-savings fees. Exclude client software subscription principal and avoid applying a second retained-share reduction to this already-retained revenue.

stages.label: Contractor delivery
stages.detail: Allocate licensing operations, savings verification, and reconciliation work across the three contractor seats. This modeled deduction leaves $380,000 before remaining costs.

stages.label: Acquisition and channel servicing
stages.detail: Budget qualified outreach, referral compensation, account onboarding, and partner-servicing costs without duplicating deductions already embedded in retained partner spreads.

stages.label: Systems and professional operations
stages.detail: Cover CRM, document storage, reconciliation tooling, bookkeeping, contract review, insurance, and operating administration. The modeled running balance becomes $255,000.

stages.label: Credit and service-loss expense
stages.detail: Model unrecovered customer exposure and service remediation as expenses. Revenue reversals already netted from the opening total must not also appear in this deduction.

stages.label: Owner net profit
stages.detail: This is the canonical annual owner-profit endpoint, not another source of revenue. Personal taxes, financing choices, and owner distributions are not separately modeled.

diagrams.title: Compare Retained Yield on a Common Spend Denominator
diagrams.subtitle: Five illustrative commercial rails measured against $100,000 of eligible annual client spend.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values are modeled retained revenue dollars, not published vendor rates or profit margins. Use comparable annual scope and exclude taxes. Rails are alternatives unless executed agreements expressly permit combined compensation without duplicate billing.
diagrams.caption: The spend denominator belongs to the customer. At a modeled 8% retained yield, $6,250,000 of eligible spend would produce $500,000 operator revenue; it would not create $6,250,000 of operator revenue.

stages.label: Microsoft CSP retained spread
stages.detail: Assume an 8% retained spread after upstream shares. Confirm current CSP economics and NCE commitment exposure; CPOR attribution alone does not establish a resale discount.

stages.label: Adobe VIP Marketplace spread
stages.detail: Assume a 10% retained spread under an authorized reseller arrangement. Validate customer eligibility, volume brackets, term alignment, and distributor deductions before quoting.

stages.label: Zoom or UCaaS residual
stages.detail: Assume a 6% annual retained residual after master-agent shares. Reconcile Telarus or Avant statements and account for installation delays, cancellations, and contracted chargebacks.

stages.label: Private GPO administrative rebate
stages.detail: Assume a 4% earned administrative rebate after member allocations. Confirm the purchasing bracket, qualifying spend, payment timing, and which party owns each rebate component.

stages.label: Renewal shared-savings fee
stages.detail: Reduce a comparable $100,000 baseline to $80,000 and earn 30% of the $20,000 verified reduction. The contracted 25%–35% fee range would produce $5,000–$7,000.

diagrams.title: Four Checks Before a Binding Commitment
diagrams.subtitle: Proceed only when authority, funding, outreach, and purchasing-group structure are documented.
diagrams.assumptions_note: These are sequential yes-or-no operating checks. Contractual licensing requirements and the internal credit policy are distinct from statutory duties. A failed check routes the account to the stated corrective action rather than silently advancing to execution.
diagrams.caption: Keep the supporting contract, funds evidence, outreach basis, and member mandate with the opportunity record. Statutes do not grant vendor transfer rights, and a customer signature does not eliminate annual vendor commitment exposure.

stages.label: Authorized licensing route?
stages.value: Yes proceed; no obtain valid authority
stages.detail: Verify the customer mandate and applicable CSP, CPOR, VIP Marketplace, Zoom, or GPO agreement. Reject unauthorized cross-tenant seat pooling; use the vendor-approved transfer process or retain the existing arrangement.

stages.label: Annual exposure fully covered?
stages.value: Yes proceed; no defer the commitment
stages.detail: Require cleared customer funding covering the committed NCE exposure and monitor ACH return or card dispute risk. Recurring debit authorization is a collection mechanism, not proof of irrevocable annual funding.

stages.label: Outreach route permitted?
stages.value: Yes proceed; no redesign the contact method
stages.detail: Apply 47 U.S.C. 227 and applicable FCC rules to calls and texts. Under 16 CFR 310.3 and 310.6(b)(7), do not treat business solicitation as exempt from specified deception prohibitions; assess relevant state calling requirements.

stages.label: GPO conduct independently defensible?
stages.value: Yes execute; no obtain structure-specific review
stages.detail: Assess competitor coordination under 15 U.S.C. 1. Preserve independent member purchasing decisions, restrict competitively sensitive information, document rebate ownership, and exclude downstream price coordination from the member arrangement.

diagrams.title: Four Core Seats, Two Explicit Scaling Additions
diagrams.subtitle: Conservative and Base use 1 FT + 3 C; Scaled uses 2 FT + 4 C.
diagrams.assumptions_note: FT means full-time and C means contractor. Numeric values indicate baseline seat occupancy: four active seats and two inactive expansion seats. Activate both expansion seats to reach the six-person Scaled pod.
diagrams.caption: The four-person pod supports the canonical $100,000 Conservative and $500,000 Base revenue cases. The six-person pod corresponds to $900,000 Scaled revenue; headcount alone does not establish demand.

stages.label: Owner and commercial lead
stages.value: One full-time core seat owns economics
stages.detail: Own vendor relationships, pricing, customer commitments, concentration limits, and cash exposure. Review exception reports instead of manually rebuilding every partner statement.

stages.label: Licensing operations specialist
stages.value: One contractor core seat owns activation
stages.detail: Validate tenant boundaries, transfer eligibility, product identifiers, commitment dates, and distributor records. Maintain evidence for every customer-authorized license change.

stages.label: Savings and procurement analyst
stages.value: One contractor core seat owns measurement
stages.detail: Build comparable incumbent baselines, test price floors, calculate contingent fees, and distinguish seat reductions from genuine like-for-like procurement savings.

stages.label: Billing and collections specialist
stages.value: One contractor core seat owns reconciliation
stages.detail: Match customer receipts, distributor charges, residual statements, and rebate settlements. Escalate funding gaps before a new annual vendor commitment is created.

stages.label: Scaled operations manager
stages.value: Add one full-time seat when scaling
stages.detail: Join the existing owner to create two full-time seats. Own delivery capacity, workflow exceptions, contractor coordination, and renewal-service continuity.

stages.label: Scaled portfolio analyst
stages.value: Add one contractor seat when scaling
stages.detail: Join the three core contractors to create four contractor seats. Expand renewal monitoring, rebate verification, and independent checks on shared-savings calculations.

diagrams.title: Four Buckets Across a $5,000–$30,000 Launch
diagrams.subtitle: Lean, working, and expanded launch budgets total $5,000, $15,000, and $30,000.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values show the $15,000 working-budget allocation. Each stage also states lean and expanded amounts for comparison. These are startup allocations, not annual operating expenses or canonical revenue scenarios; no bucket finances customer subscription principal.
diagrams.caption: The working allocation is $4,500 + $3,000 + $4,500 + $3,000 = $15,000. Monthly opex remains the supplied $1,500–$9,500 planning range. Protect runway through the 1–3 month first-deal window without using customer-designated funds for brokerage expenses.

stages.label: Partner and contract setup
stages.detail: Allocate 30% to agreement review, customer mandates, bookkeeping setup, partner onboarding work, and insurance setup. Vendor-specific deposits require separate verification.

stages.label: Systems and reconciliation
stages.detail: Allocate 20% to CRM configuration, access-controlled document storage, statement imports, renewal tracking, and audit-ready reconciliation templates before purchasing custom integrations.

stages.label: Evidence-led acquisition
stages.detail: Allocate 30% to vertical prospect research, buyer interviews, permissioned outreach, and initial contract audits. Measure qualified opportunities rather than purchased contact volume.

stages.label: Brokerage liquidity reserve
stages.detail: Allocate 20% to brokerage timing gaps and operating contingencies. Keep this reserve distinct from customer prefunding and increase runway if sales or settlement takes longer.

diagrams.title: A 30-Day Sprint to an Execution-Ready Brokerage
diagrams.subtitle: Build evidence and operating readiness before forecasting collected residuals.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The four milestones span Days 1–30. Activities use authorized project resources and customer-provided records. Partner onboarding, renewal timing, and vendor activation can extend beyond this sprint; the canonical first-deal range is 1–3 months.
diagrams.caption: Finish the sprint with a defined niche, verified economics, executable documents, and a reconciled pilot or documented activation schedule. Do not label quoted savings, unsigned rebates, or future residuals as recognized revenue.

stages.label: Days 1-7
stages.value: Choose one niche and verify partner routes
stages.detail: Select a repeatable buyer segment, obtain current partner terms, define excluded license arrangements, and build a retained-revenue worksheet separating subscription principal from operator consideration.

stages.label: Days 8-14
stages.value: Collect evidence and test comparable economics
stages.detail: Request permissioned renewal contracts, normalize product scope, test vendor price floors, and calculate prospective shared-savings fees. Document why each candidate passes or fails the four pre-commitment checks.

stages.label: Days 15-21
stages.value: Execute mandates and establish funded readiness
stages.detail: Finalize compensation terms, member rebate allocation, customer authority, and permitted transfer steps. Verify funding before annual commitments and configure distributor or master-agent statement reconciliation.

stages.label: Days 22-30
stages.value: Reconcile a pilot and schedule remaining activation
stages.detail: Complete one authorized pilot when vendor timing permits, or record the dated activation dependency. Reconcile earned consideration, inspect exception handling, and compare forecast contribution with the Base-Case cost structure.
